fix(release): require the Release-As footer inside the commit override block (#672)

Release-please replaces the merged commit message with the contents of a pull
request's BEGIN_COMMIT_OVERRIDE block on a squash-merge. A footer placed after
END_COMMIT_OVERRIDE is therefore never parsed, and the failure is silent: the
release is prepared at the computed version with no error, no warning, and no
log line naming the override.

That is why the overrides in #670 and #671 did nothing. Release-please's own dry
run showed it: the changelog entries for both delivery commits carry the text of
their override blocks rather than their commit subjects, so the message it
parsed never contained the footer. The earlier theory about a wrapped line was
wrong, and re-sending the same shape a second time was the cost of guessing
instead of running the tool.

Validate placement, which is the only point where the mistake is visible.
Correct the pre-existing test that asserted the wrong placement, and record the
rule in the release-workflow spec and the release runbook.

Release-As: 1.11.0
